text: Given the significant elevation in alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin, along with the ultrasound finding of an enlarged gallbladder without stones, this pattern strongly suggests obstructive jaundice, likely due to a malignancy in the head of the pancreas or the ampulla of Vater. text: The ultrasound findings of an enlarged, stone-free gallbladder (Courvoisier's sign) combined with painless jaundice strongly point towards a pancreatic head malignancy blocking the common bile duct. text: The normal CT scan makes a pancreatic mass unlikely, so I must consider other causes of obstructive jaundice with Courvoisier's sign, such as cholangiocarcinoma or ampullary carcinoma.
